record.paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
record.original_question: Is there a simple general construction that produces graphs with many interlacing values for subgraph centrality, rather than relying on ad hoc computational search?

evidence.quote: A related, more informal problem is the following: is there a simple way to construct graphs with many interlacing values?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices, with adjacency matrix $A$. The subgraph centrality of a vertex $v\in V$ is defined by
$$\mathrm{SC}(v) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(A^k)_{vv}}{k!} \;=\; \bigl(e^{A}\bigr)_{vv}.$$
Equivalently, if $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ are the eigenvalues of $A$ with an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_n$, then
$$\mathrm{SC}(v) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{n} \varphi_j(v)^2\, e^{\lambda_j}.$$
Order the vertices so that $\mathrm{SC}(v_1)\ge \mathrm{SC}(v_2)\ge \cdots \ge \mathrm{SC}(v_n)$, and consider any vertex invariant $f:V\to\mathbb{R}$ (for instance the degree, eigenvector centrality, or closeness centrality). We say that an unordered pair $\{u,w\}$ of vertices is an interlacing pair for $\mathrm{SC}$ and $f$ if
$$\mathrm{SC}(u) < \mathrm{SC}(w) \quad\text{and}\quad f(u) > f(w),$$
i.e. the ranking induced by $\mathrm{SC}$ disagrees with the ranking induced by $f$ on $\{u,w\}$. The number of such pairs is called the number of interlacing values of $G$ (with respect to $f$).

Problem. Exhibit a simple, explicit general construction (i.e. a deterministic recipe taking parameters such as $n$ or a base graph and producing a family of graphs) that yields graphs with arbitrarily many interlacing values for subgraph centrality, without relying on ad hoc computer search.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search on subgraph centrality and interlacing constructions did not surface any publication providing a simple general construction of graphs with many interlacing values for subgraph centrality. No follow-up work resolving this informal question was identified, but the absence of search hits is inconclusive, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Subgraph Centrality in Complex Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Subgraph centrality of a node is the sum of weighted closed walks of all lengths starting and ending at that node.
status_evidence.claim: Defines subgraph centrality but does not provide constructions producing many interlacing values.

status_evidence.title: A centrality measure for cycles and subgraphs II
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses centrality measures based on subgraphs.
status_evidence.claim: Does not address constructions of graphs with many interlacing values for subgraph centrality.
